title: Check yourself: A fixed chain or an adaptive plan

questions.stem: A team reviews a fourteen-file change by sending all the files in one request. The comments are deep for the first files and thin for the last ones, and a changed signature in one file is never matched against its callers elsewhere. Which restructuring fits best?

options.text: Give each source its own examination, then run a pass over what they concluded
options.says: Each file gets a full review in its own context, and a second pass sees the relations.

options.text: Send the same single request three times and merge the answers into one report
options.says: Ruled out because repetition keeps what causes the problem: "A request that holds a dozen files spends that budget on text before the review begins".

options.text: Split the change into two halves of seven files and review each half in one request
options.says: Ruled out because halves keep the dilution and still hide the relations between the halves: "The exam calls the effect attention dilution".

options.text: Keep the single request and add an instruction to treat every file with equal care
options.says: Ruled out because an instruction does not change what fills the context: "LLM performance degrades as context fills".

origin.section: Why a review is split in two

questions.stem: A team must add tests to a large legacy codebase that it does not know. Which order of work does the exam expect?

options.text: List the directories, give each one a test task, then run the tasks in order
options.says: Ruled out because a fixed order cannot follow the findings: "a pipeline that marches through steps that no longer make sense".

options.text: Write the whole test plan first, order it by file size, then run it to its end
options.says: Ruled out because a plan made before any ground truth is a guess: "the plan is made before any ground truth exists".

options.text: Map the structure and rank by impact, then re-plan as dependencies appear
options.says: An open-ended task is mapped first and planned from what is found.

options.text: Take the largest files first, write tests for them, then continue down the list
options.says: Ruled out because size is not impact: the task is "mapped first, then the high-impact areas are found".
